sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different context than the problems below.

items.prompt: Relationship A: x: 0, 1, 2, 3 y: 1, 3, 5, 7. Relationship B: x: 0, 1, 2, 3 y: 7, 6, 5, 4. At which x-value do the two relationships have the same y-value?

steps: Compare the y-values in each table row by row.
At x = 2, Relationship A gives 5 and Relationship B also gives 5.
No other row has matching y-values, so x = 2 is the answer.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Solve the system: y = -x + 15 and y = -9x + 143. In which quadrant does the intersection point lie, or does it lie on an axis?

Solve the system:
y = -5x + 19
10x - 7y = 47
Use substitution to find the solution (x, y).

Solve the system:
9x + 3y = -114
-9x - y = 92
Use elimination to find the solution (x, y).
Classify the system: y = 6x + 17 and y = 6x - 17. Does it have one solution, no solution, or infinitely many solutions?
The reference equation is y = 2x + 23. Which of these equations, paired with the reference, would give the system infinitely many solutions?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: These are meant to be hard. Show the reasoning even if you do not finish.

items.prompt: Plan A charges a $60 flat fee plus $7 per month. Plan B charges a $50 flat fee plus $9 per month. After how many months do the two plans cost the same, and what is that cost?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Plan A charges a $52 flat fee plus $14 per week. Plan B charges a $88 flat fee plus $2 per week. The solution to the system is (3, 94). What does this solution represent?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: System: y = -6x - 78 and y = -8x - 104. Does the point (-12, -5) satisfy both equations, fail one, or fail both?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
